analysis.investment_thesis: Anlon reports impressive accounting profits (ROE 25.5%, ROCE 38%) but has burned cash every single year (OCF 0/4 positive, FCF -23 Cr in 2025 against a reported PAT of 21 Cr) — the earnings aren't real cash. At a recent listing with P/E 17.75 and EV/EBITDA ~11x on a working-capital-heavy small-cap API maker, the price reflects optimism that the cycle and the balance sheet simply don't support.
key_strengths: Reported operating margin 33.7% and ROCE 38% are genuinely high if sustainable
key_risks: OCF negative 4/4 years; PAT-to-cash conversion is broken — classic working-capital trap
Revenue lumpy (57→113→67→120 Cr) — no demonstrated through-cycle stability
Recent equity raise (equity 21→80 Cr) suggests IPO-peak capital gathering; D/E still 0.27 with only 1 Cr cash
red_flags: PAT 21 Cr vs FCF -23 Cr in FY25 — a 44 Cr gap is a major earnings-quality warning
Zero years of positive operating cash flow across the shown history
Tiny float, freshly-listed micro-cap in a hot pharma/API theme — textbook late-cycle IPO setup
analysis.detailed_analysis: Second-level thinking here is simple: the first-level story is "high-growth Indian API maker, 28% revenue CAGR, 38% ROCE, reasonable 17x P/E." The second-level reality is that every rupee of reported profit has been more than consumed by receivables and inventory — FY25 shows 21 Cr PAT but -23 Cr operating cash flow, a 44 Cr quality gap. Financing cash flow (+19 Cr) and the recent equity infusion (equity jumped from 21 to 80 Cr) are what's keeping the lights on, not the business. In API/intermediate manufacturing, working-capital-heavy growth without cash generation is how small pharma companies blow up when a customer delays payment or a cycle turns.
